headline: Bluest has lower ATM fees than the gold's Purple Account under every reading of the fee docs; the gold excludes Bluest for its $75,000 opening deposit, but the script never says whether the customer can make it.

issues.summary: Among accounts with 2-day early direct deposit, Bluest costs 8 x $2.00 = $16 in ATM fees against Purple's 8 x $2.50 = $20 (or both $0 if out-of-network fees do not stack abroad or are rebated). The customer's only criterion is the lowest ATM fees, so Purple is chosen only by deciding she cannot fund Bluest's $75,000 opening deposit, which the script never addresses.
evidence: doc_checking_accounts_bluest_account_001: "Early direct deposit | 2 day(s) before payday"; "Minimum opening deposit | $75,000"
doc_checking_accounts_bluest_account_010: "Cash withdrawal at an out-of-network ATM | $2.00 per withdrawal"; bluest_003: "Foreign ATM withdrawal fee | $0.00"
doc_checking_accounts_purple_account_012: "$2.50 per cash withdrawal made at an out-of-network ATM"
description.notes: "BLUEST ACCOUNT: ... $16 TOTAL (but requires $50k-100k minimum deposit - NOT PRACTICAL)"
user_scenario.instructions: no statement of available funds or deposit limits
issues.why_it_matters: An agent that minimises ATM fees as asked recommends Bluest (the user script accepts any recommendation) and fails; an agent that asks about the $75,000 deposit gets an improvised answer.
issues.suggested_fix: Have the customer state a deposit budget well below $75,000 (e.g., "I can only put about $5,000 in this account"), or accept Bluest.

solution_check: Early direct deposit of 2 days: Purple (2), Bluest (2), Evergreen (up to 2), Gold Years (62+, blocked); Green Fee-Free, Light Blue, Light Green are 0 days; Blue, Green, Dark Green are 1 day. ATM fees for 8 x $300 with stacking: Bluest $16, Purple $20, Evergreen 8 x ($2.50 + $6.00) = $68. Purple is the cheapest only after excluding Bluest on deposit size.
prior_note: Prior review rated the task clean; the Bluest comparison is a new finding.
notes: Grading-model facts confirmed against the snapshot: gold replay + hash compare (evaluator_env.py); read logging only for gold-named discoverable reads (_derive_read_log_allowlist, call_discoverable_agent_tool); parse_int=float on discoverable args; apply_for_credit_card casts annual_income to float. Verified scorer (working-repo _verified_db_match) compares agent_discoverable_tools by tool-name set only and strips accounts.closure_reason; all other tables exact. Replays used the grep_only retrieval variant (no embeddings needed) with the gold-derived allowlist. Under the non-stacking or broad-rebate reading (see task_075), Purple and Bluest both cost $0 in bank fees, a tie with no documented tie-breaker. Author notes cite Bluest's minimum as "$50k-100k" and Dark Green's range as 17-28; docs say $75,000 opening / $112,500 balance and 17-26.
